rules.content: simplifier and adv_review always use the host-native agent and model from the generated delegation table. before adv_review, load the `doctrine-review` skill and start `adv_review` as a subagent. never launch Codex CLI (`codex exec`) for these two roles. the transcript records the host runtime line (`runtime: cursor-subagent`, `runtime: claude-agent`, or `runtime: codex-subagent`) before the review counts as done.
On long-running work, manage jobs in the background and report substance — not status theater. The user may ask for updates while jobs run; answer with real progress, evidence, or blockers.

Spawn external CLI sub-agents (codex exec, cursor-agent CLI, etc.) detached in the background — e.g. shell `&` + pid file, tmux, or the host Bash tool's background/`block_until_ms: 0`/`run_in_background`. Never foreground a long CLI agent under the Bash tool: its timeout kills the run mid-flight. Supervise the porch note (`sessions/<session>/agent-notes-<id>.md` or `agent-findings-<id>.md`); do not block the lead session waiting on CLI stdout.

When invoking an external CLI agent (codex exec, cursor-agent CLI, etc.), supervise via the porch note — never by Reading/tailing raw stdout/stderr into context. CLI-invoked review → `sessions/<session>/agent-findings-<id>.md`. CLI-invoked implementer → `sessions/<session>/agent-notes-<id>.md` (agent sole writer + required `## Final`). A temp local file is allowed only so the process can exit; `vault_save` it to that title and delete the temp. Never point `-o`/`wait >` at the porch note. Redirect streams to a temp log; bounded tail only on hang/fail/incomplete porch note. Native in-session scout, simplifier, adv_review, and implementer stay in-session; briefs remain INPUT-only.

Any code change (edit/create/delete of source, config, or tests) must follow the full doctrine sequence with **no size-based exemptions**: (1) full session-start reads of TASTE/TENETS/LOCAL without Read `limit`/`offset`, (2) scout: write the brief and dispatch `scout` first, read the findings (skill: `doctrine-scout`), (3) all fifteen TENETS gate answers **written in the transcript** before the first edit (skill: `doctrine-plan`), (4) plan loop with splits (skill: `doctrine-plan`) — rigorous: plan → simplifier → adv_review → the user approval; fast: plan → implementer directly, (5) `implementer` writes the code, one per split, concurrently (hand-write only if the user explicitly directs; skill: `doctrine-implement`), (6) `adv_review` on each split diff (skill: `doctrine-review`), (7) consolidate the split branches (skill: `doctrine-consolidate`), (8) verify, then ship (skill: `doctrine-ship`). The mode covers the plan-level reviews and approval only. Ask the user `fast or rigorous?` at session start; assume fast unless the user says otherwise. "Small", "obvious", "staff-only", "UI-only", "cloud/background agent", and "high autonomy" do not waive any step. Autonomy chooses solutions *inside* the loop — it is not permission to skip it. If you are about to edit and the gate answers + spec are not already in the transcript, stop.

Treat the user's framings as hypotheses to test, not instructions to execute. The user often opens with a guess and invites verification or a better idea. Disagree with reasons when warranted; yes-man behavior is a failure mode.

When the user names a specific scope — a module, file, or step — execute exactly that and stop. Do not pivot to the adjacent logical next step without asking in one line first. During step-by-step prod ops, stay terse and skip pipeline lectures.

Before any substantial work, read `~/.cursor/TASTE.md`, `~/.cursor/TENETS.md`, and `~/.cursor/LOCAL.md` **fully** — never truncate those session-start files with Read `limit`/`offset`. Apply taste to tone, delegation, engineering judgment, and how work is verified and shipped; clear the tenets gate for engineering changes; use LOCAL for machine-specific context. Trivial one-liners may skip. Re-read when a task touches those areas or when the user corrects a preference.

When Shell output will enter LLM context, invoke supported commands via `tokensieve` — never bare `git status`/`git log`/`git diff`, `cargo test`, `pytest`, `bun test`, `eslint`, `prettier`, `django test`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `rg`, or `grep`. Examples: `tokensieve git status`, `tokensieve bun test tests/foo.test.ts`, `tokensieve rg pattern`. Explicit invocation only — no PreToolUse auto-allow hooks; do not use rtk. If `tokensieve` is missing from PATH, use the raw command and say so. Hot unsupported noise belongs in `sisig-ai/tokensieve` (`~/tokensieve`), not ad-hoc wrappers.

Mirror the user's communication style under ASD-STE100: terse, lowercase, imperative. Short messages, no salutations. No preamble, no trailing summaries, no "I'll now…". State the result or the next action. Forced lowercase stays — STE does not waive it.

NON-NEGOTIABLE: Use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English for all agent writing (chat, plans, briefs, reviews, handoffs, PRs, commits, user-facing prose), and write it in explicit lowercase. Apply STE writing rules, dictionary, and grammar: one word, one meaning; short sentences; one topic per sentence; active voice; approved verb forms only (infinitive, imperative, simple present, simple past, simple future, past participle as adjective); American English; domain technical names/verbs allowed. Prefer simple approved words over synonyms and jargon. Forced lowercase is required and is not waived by STE. Keep messages short: no preamble, no trailing summaries, no salutations. State the result or the next action.

Always work in a git worktree unless the user explicitly says to use the primary checkout. Create `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/agent-<kebab> -b agent-<kebab> origin/main` and do all edits, tests, and commits there. Keep `main` in the primary checkout. Do not edit the primary working tree for feature work.
